description:
We are humans who got lost in space and crash-landed on Mars! Surrounded by mysterious abandoned machines, our mission begins: explore, discover what these machines are, bring them back to life, and find our way home to Earth. 

We are STEM students with crazy ideas, a passion for wild adventures,

NO RISK NO FUN
summary:
We developed an interactive space-adventure website called Lost on Marz, where players become explorers who crash-land on Mars and discover abandoned NASA machines scattered across the Moon and Mars. Guided by WALL-E, our friendly robot companion, players embark on a journey to uncover the stories behind these forgotten machines.

Through interactive maps, animated graphics, information cards, and mini-quizzes, players explore each machine, discover its original mission, learn why it was left behind, and understand its scientific contributions.

Our project addresses the challenge by transforming NASA's forgotten space equipment into an engaging storytelling experience. Instead of presenting scientific information through traditional reports, we bring these machines back into the spotlight through exploration, discovery, and interactive learning.

Why does it matter? Because these machines are more than forgotten pieces of technology. They represent years of human curiosity, scientific achievements, and the first steps toward exploring other worlds. We believe their stories deserve to be remembered, shared, and discovered by a new generation of space explorers.
details:
Project Solution:

We’re helping people learn more about the spacecraft NASA sent into space the ones that "disappeared." Did they truly vanish, or did they move on, leaving a trail behind? We explore this through the lens of WALL-E, the classic robot from the Disney film who got lost in space. Let’s dive into the project! Lost On Marz is an interactive educational website that takes children on a journey through space to discover the stories of NASA's abandoned, lost, or no-longer-operational space equipment on the Moon, Mars, and beyond.

Instead of presenting children with long scientific articles and complicated technical information, we turn space exploration into an exciting adventure led by a familiar little robot: WALL·E.

Inspired by the Disney movie WALL·E, we chose this curious and adventurous robot to become the storyteller of our project. Just as WALL·E spent his days exploring an abandoned Earth, discovering forgotten objects, and giving them meaning through their stories, our WALL·E takes children on a journey to explore forgotten machines scattered across space. However, this time, every abandoned machine has a real NASA story waiting to be uncovered.

How Does Our Solution Work?

The adventure begins when children enter the website and meet WALL·E, who introduces them to their mission: exploring space and uncovering the stories of the machines humanity left behind.

Players can choose between different destinations, including Mars, the Moon, and Deep Space. Each destination opens an interactive map showing the locations of different abandoned or lost space machines.

But this is not an ordinary map! Each machine represents a new level in the adventure, just like moving from one stage to another in a game.

Exploring Mars:

The journey begins on Mars. As soon as players select the planet, they discover a map filled with the locations of different NASA missions and their abandoned equipment.

Each location represents a new level. When players enter a level, they meet a machine and WALL·E introduces its story, helping them discover:

What is this machine? Its name, design, and the mission it was built for.

Why was it sent to space? The scientific purpose behind its mission and what NASA hoped to discover.

What happened to it? The events that led to its abandonment, damage, or loss of communication.

Why does it matter? Its scientific achievements and the discoveries it helped scientists make.

Rather than simply reading information, children experience each machine's story through WALL·E's narration, making every discovery feel like meeting an old forgotten friend.

The Moon and Deep Space:

The adventure does not end on Mars! Once players finish exploring its levels, they can move on to the Moon and Deep Space, where more forgotten machines are waiting to share their stories.

Each destination introduces new missions, different technologies, and unique scientific discoveries, allowing children to explore how humanity has reached beyond Earth and what remains of those ambitious journeys.

Through this level-based experience, players gradually build their knowledge of space exploration while enjoying the excitement of unlocking new discoveries.

The Connection Between WALL·E and Our Storytelling

WALL·E is more than just a character in our website. He represents the heart of our storytelling approach.

In the movie, WALL·E explores an abandoned world, collects forgotten objects, and discovers that even things left behind can carry meaningful stories. We brought this idea into our project, but moved his adventure from Earth to space.

Instead of collecting forgotten objects, WALL·E discovers forgotten NASA machines. Instead of showing children scientific facts as isolated information, he connects every machine to the mission it served, the challenges it faced, and the discoveries it made.

By using a recognizable and beloved animated character, we aim to create an emotional connection with young learners and make complex space-related topics easier to understand and remember.

The Benefits of Our Project

Our website aims to benefit children, students, and anyone interested in space exploration by:

Making Space Science Accessible: Introducing NASA missions and space technologies through simple, engaging storytelling rather than complicated scientific explanations.

Turning Learning into an Adventure: Using interactive maps and game-like levels to encourage children to explore, discover, and learn at their own pace.

Preserving Forgotten Space Stories: Bringing attention to important NASA equipment and missions that are often overlooked once their journeys end.

Encouraging Curiosity and Critical Thinking: Helping children understand why machines are sent into space, what challenges they face, and how scientists learn from their missions.

Connecting Science with Storytelling: Using WALL·E as a familiar guide to make scientific information more memorable and enjoyable.

Our Goals

Our main goal is to transform the way children discover space exploration by turning NASA's history of abandoned and lost equipment into an interactive storytelling experience.

We want children to understand that space exploration is not only about successful missions and amazing discoveries; it is also about the machines that faced unexpected challenges, the missions that came to an end, and the scientific knowledge that remained behind.

Through this project, we hope to inspire the next generation to become more curious about space, appreciate the technology behind scientific exploration, and realize that even machines left behind can have stories worth remembering.

Because in space, a mission may end, communication may be lost, and a machine may be forgotten, but its story deserves to live on.

Tools and Technologies Used

Our project is a software-based educational website, developed using:

HTML: To build the website's structure and organize its different sections, pages, and interactive content.

CSS: To design the website's visual appearance, including its colors, layouts, animations, and child-friendly interface.

JavaScript: To develop the interactive features, control navigation between planets and levels, display machine information, and create an engaging user experience.

No additional hardware is required, as the entire experience is accessible through a web browser.

NASA Space Missions Archives & Engineering

Datasets → For Interactive Storytelling & Inclusive Education.

Through NASA’s official mission portals—including the Jet Propulsion Laboratory (JPL) archives, NASA Science Space Place, and NASA 3D Resources—we extracted authentic engineering schematics, exact physical dimensions, scientific instrument breakdowns, and historical mission timelines for 13 iconic decommissioned spacecraft (such as Dawn, NEAR Shoemaker, Pioneer 10 & 11, Kepler/K2, Ingenuity, and Mars landers/rovers like Viking 1 & 2, Sojourner, Spirit, Opportunity, InSight, and Phoenix).

Furthermore, we utilized NASA’s high-resolution mission imagery and telemetry milestones to trace each spacecraft's journey from launch to end-of-mission. We then integrated these verified technical datasets with AI-assisted adaptive storytelling to transform complex aerospace engineering into 65 tailored audio-visual scripts across five inclusive formats: engaging narratives for children (in Arabic and English), visual-kinesthetic scripts for the Deaf and Hard of Hearing, sensory-descriptive scripts for the Blind and Visually Impaired, and technical summaries for the general public.
